messages:
maya: quick sync — we need to standardize GPU signals for Hosted + Dedicated pools before I start dashboard mockups. core metrics: SM occupancy, per-GPU mem RSS, per-pool queue_depth, and headroom.
jun: +1. can you list the exact metric names we should expose? also need labels (pool_type, pool_id, model, tenant) so product can slice.
anika: from runtime side: SM occupancy should be "active_wavefronts / sm_count" sampled per-GPU. proposing metric name: `rwi_runtime_sm_active_waves_total` and `rwi_runtime_sm_count`. keep them simple and numeric.
liam: for memory let's export `rwi_gpu_memory_rss_bytes` and `rwi_gpu_memory_total_bytes` (both per-device). we can also derive pct used in the dashboard.
rob-b: queue depth varies by layer (inference queue vs postprocess). suggest `rwi_pool_queue_depth{queue="inference|post"}` and `rwi_pool_headroom_tokens` as best-effort. careful about cardinality on `model` label.
product-sr: product needs a per-tenant view for Dedicated (to show committed vs used). add `tenant_id` label but only on Dedicated metrics (privacy). how do we gate that? :thinking_face:
anika: we can add `tenant_id` when running in private/dedicated; Hosted will omit tenant_id. runtime will ensure label cardinality stays bounded (hashed bucket for very high-card tenants?).
jun: telemetry question — retention & downsample strategy? we can't keep per-second SM occupancy for 30d at full res.
telemetry-bot: note: ingestion costs spike if retention/resolution high. recommend 1s->1m rollup after 24h for high-card metrics. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
liam: agreed. propose raw 1s for 6h, 10s for 24h, 1m thereafter. that covers spike troubleshooting and long-term trends.
maya: sample PromQLs for panels so infra can validate names:
```
# per-GPU SM occupancy pct
(sum by (gpu_id) (rwi_runtime_sm_active_waves_total{pool_type=~"hosted|dedicated"})
 / sum by (gpu_id) (rwi_runtime_sm_count{pool_type=~"hosted|dedicated"})) * 100
\n# per-pool queue depth
sum by (pool_id, queue) (rwi_pool_queue_depth{pool_type="hosted"})
\n# per-tenant Dedicated committed vs used memory (bytes)
sum by (tenant_id) (rwi_gpu_memory_total_bytes{pool_type="dedicated"})
 vs
sum by (tenant_id) (rwi_gpu_memory_rss_bytes{pool_type="dedicated"})
```
rob-b: small ask — add `gpu_arch` label (a100/v100/mi250) so we can stratify perf. not optional for model perf dashboards.
anika: ok but we must keep `gpu_arch` low-card and only on device-level metrics (not per-pod).
product-sr: UX question: when a tenant hits committed capacity, what's the observable that should trigger an alert or soft-quotas message?
liam: alert = sustained (5m) headroom_tokens < threshold OR queue_depth > X for 2m. soft quota path = show modal in Console w/ suggested mitigation (switch to dedicated, reduce batch size).
maya: rollout plan: this week we agree metric names + labels. next week runtime/infra add metrics to staging. liam will own the dashboard (staging -> prod rollout).
liam: I can own owner ship. will create the staging dashboard and shared link.
jun: engineering owners: runtime = anika, infra/telemetry = jun/telemetry-bot, dashboard = liam, product follow-up = product-sr. I'll add to the repo checklist.
deploy-bot: dashboard-ci: created PR rwi/infra-dashboards#342, scheduled sync job to validate metrics in staging.
maya: thanks — next steps: 1) anika add metrics + labels to runtime PR, 2) jun confirm retention/rollup config, 3) liam wire staging dashboard, 4) product confirm alert copy. meeting if needed after PRs. :white_check_mark:
product-sr: can we include a short blurb in Console docs about what 'SM occupancy' means? end-users will ask.
maya: yes — I'll draft wording: "SM occupancy = percent of streaming multiprocessors actively scheduling inference work; high occupancy often correlates with better throughput but may increase latency for bursty traffic."
liam: ping me when the staging PR is merged. I'll populate panels and add annotations for rollout. :eyes:
maya: closing loop: added this thread to the eng-platform board. will post PR links here. thanks everyone. :rocket:
